name: clicklock dev
iocPatterns: Terminal loading animation mimicking Cloudflare progress bar
Zero‑detection malware sample posted to VirusTotal
Phishing pages distributed via compromised WordPress domains and Telegram infrastructure
Forced password entry required to unlock the system
Known phishing domains: update-check.com, claudecodedoc.squarespace.com, macclean.craft.me
Hidden directory pattern $HOME/.cacheb/ used for stolen modules
keyCapabilities: Harvests cryptocurrency wallet addresses across multiple blockchains
Steals credentials from browsers, extensions, password managers, desktop wallets and macOS Keychain
Collects shell history and FTP credentials
Locks system usage by forcefully terminating visible processes until the user enters a correct password
Mimics Cloudflare progress bars in terminal to deceive users
Copies Keychain database after user grants Full Disk Access
Archives stolen data into ZIP files for staging
Exfiltrates data via Telegram bot and compromised domains
Imposes persistence through LaunchAgents and hidden background services
Employs PowerShell and Unix shell scripts for execution
Uses obfuscated code, file masquerading and indicator removal for evasion
Captures credentials through GUI input capture and forced authentication
Discards critical services to disrupt normal operation
recommendedActions: Block outbound connections to known malicious domains (ClickFix phishing sites, compromised WordPress hosts, update‑check.com, panalobet.ph, store.grafsynergy.com) and Telegram bot endpoints.
Monitor and block GSocket traffic from macOS endpoints to prevent backdoor communication.
Enforce Gatekeeper, System Integrity Protection, and strict privilege controls; restrict Terminal full‑disk access permissions unless absolutely necessary.
Disable or monitor LaunchAgents under ~/Library/LaunchAgents to detect persistence scripts.
Deploy endpoint detection that flags rapid termination of user‑visible processes and background services masquerading as reverse shells.
Educate employees on phishing techniques that mimic Cloudflare captchas and safe command‑execution practices.
Monitor for abnormal keychain access, Chrome Safe Storage credential theft, and GUI input capture events.
Apply regular macOS updates to patch kernel vulnerabilities and enforce automatic updates.
Implement web filtering or DNS blocking of malicious URLs used by the actor.
campaignsText: Starting in May 2026, ClickLock Dev has compromised over one hundred macOS users across 33 countries. The majority of victims lie in European nations, with notable infections reported from North America and the Middle East. Primary delivery vectors are compromised WordPress domains (e.g., panalobet.ph) and Telegram‑based phishing pages that mislead operators into executing terminal commands. Once deployed, the malware establishes long‑lived persistence via LaunchAgents, exfiltrates stolen assets over Telegram and custom C2 servers, and disrupts normal system operation through aggressive process termination loops, thereby forcing user compliance and reducing visible alerts.
description: ClickLock Dev is a financially motivated macOS actor deploying ClickFix‑style phishing pages that trick users into running malicious terminal commands. The resultant payload, ClickLock Stealer, harvests browser and wallet credentials, installs a persistent GSocket backdoor, and locks the system until an attacker‑provided password is entered. Over 100 victims across 33 countries have been affected through compromised WordPress sites and Telegram‑based command and control channels.
goals: ClickLock Dev’s primary objective is monetary enrichment through automated extraction of browser, password manager, and cryptocurrency wallet credentials. The actor targets sectors that routinely store high‑value digital assets—financial services, media, manufacturing, and defense—and focuses on a geographically diverse victim set spanning Europe, North America, and the Middle East. By coercing user interaction to gain full‑disk access, the threat actor ensures persistence while minimizing privilege escalation hurdles, thereby maximizing data return for relatively low effort per target.
